steps.body: Add 47 + 25 and the ones pile up: 7 + 5 = **12 ones** — too many for one spot, which holds at most 9. So the trading post from chapter 1 opens: 10 of those ones trade up into 1 ten, leaving 2 ones behind. "Carrying" isn't a new skill — it's the ten-for-one trade, running uphill.
Watch the overflow and the trade, one panel at a time.

panels.title: The ones overflow
panels.body: Ones first: 7 + 5 = 12 ones. But a spot holds at most 9 — the ones spot is overflowing.

panels.title: The trade
panels.body: Ten of the 12 ones trade up into 1 ten; 2 ones stay behind. Nothing was lost — 12 ones and 1-ten-2-ones are the same amount, repackaged.

panels.title: Finish the tens
panels.body: Tens now: 4 + 2, plus the 1 traded ten = 7 tens. Answer: 72. That little "carry 1" you write? It's the trade receipt.

widget.continueFeedback: Keep going — the trade happens in the next panel.
widget.successFeedback: Overflow → trade up → count the receipt with the tens. 47 + 25 = 72.

predict.prompt: 47 + 25: the ones pile makes 7 + 5 = 12. What must happen?

options.label: Ten of them trade up — the answer is 72
Write 12 in the ones spot — the answer is 612
Nothing — 12 fits in the ones spot fine

predict.reveal: Twelve ones overflow a spot that holds nine: ten bundle into a rod, joining 4 + 2 to make 7 tens — 72. Writing 612 records the raw pile without trading: right as an amount, wrong as a numeral.

explanationVariants: 8 + 6 = 14 ones — an overflow. Ten of them trade into 1 ten, and the little 1 records that trade above the tens column.
The carry mark is a receipt: it reminds you a ten arrived from the ones' trade, waiting to be counted with the tens.

widget.prompt: In 38 + 26, a little 1 appears above the tens column. What is it?

options.label: A trade receipt: 8+6=14 ones, ten traded up
options.feedback: The ones overflowed past 9, so ten of them became one ten — the little 1 is that ten, waiting in line.

options.label: Just a decoration that teachers like to add
options.feedback: It carries real value — a whole ten! Skip it and the answer drops by 10 (54 instead of 64).

options.label: A rule: always write a 1 when you're adding
options.feedback: Try 41 + 23: ones make just 4 — no overflow, no trade, no little 1. It appears only when a spot's sum passes 9.

options.label: The 1 came from the number 38 — but it didn't
options.feedback: Right — it's not copied from anywhere. It's NEW packaging: ten loose ones bundled into a single ten.

steps.body: When does the trade fire? **Only on overflow.** Check each spot's sum: 9 or less, write it and move on; 10 or more, trade ten of them up and keep the rest. 41 + 23 needs no trade at all (ones: 1 + 3 = 4). The trade is a response, not a habit.

explanationVariants: Ones: 7 + 5 = 12 → 2 stays, 1 ten trades up. Tens: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. Answer 72.
Jump-check it: 47 + 20 = 67, + 5 = 72 — the trade answer and the jump answer agree.

widget.prompt: 47 + 25 = ? Build the sum in standard form with rods and cubes.

commonBuilds.feedback: 62 dropped the trade receipt — the ten that came up from the ones never joined the tens count: 4 + 2 + 1, not 4 + 2.
612 wrote all 12 ones in the ones spot. One digit per spot: trade ten of them for a rod — 7 tens, 2 ones.
71 lost a one in the shuffle: 12 ones leave 2 behind after trading, not 1.

widget.missFeedback: Ones first (7 + 5 = 12 → trade), then tens plus the receipt: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. The sum is 72.
widget.successFeedback: 7 rods and 2 cubes — the twelve ones traded ten of themselves into the tens column.

steps.body: Two overflows, two trades, one chain.
hints: Ones first: 6 + 7 — does the trade fire?
13 ones → 3 stay, 1 ten trades up. Now the tens: 3 + 8 + 1.
12 tens is ALSO an overflow — ten of them trade into 1 hundred. Hundreds: 2 + 1 + 1.
explanationVariants: Ones: 13 → trade (write 3). Tens: 3 + 8 + 1 = 12 → trade again (write 2). Hundreds: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Answer 423.
Guard it: 236 + 187 ≈ 200 + 200 = 400 — and 423 sits right beside the guard.

widget.prompt: 236 + 187 = ? Build the sum in standard form with flats, rods, and cubes.

commonBuilds.feedback: 413 lost the FIRST receipt — the ten from the ones' trade never joined the tens (3 + 8 + 1 = 12, not 11).
323 lost the SECOND receipt — the hundred from the tens' trade never joined the hundreds (2 + 1 + 1 = 4, not 3).
313 dropped BOTH receipts. Every trade sends its value one spot up — two trades, two receipts, both must be counted.

widget.missFeedback: Chain the trades: ones overflow feeds the tens; the tens overflow feeds the hundreds. 236 + 187 = 423.
widget.successFeedback: 4 flats, 2 rods, 3 cubes — both trade receipts landed where they belonged.

steps.body: Carrying is just trading — and you can see it now.
takeaways: A spot holds at most 9; a bigger sum trades ten of itself one spot up.
The carry mark is a trade receipt — always count it with the next spot.
Trades chain: an overflow in the tens sends a hundred upstairs the same way.
steps.teaser: subtraction runs the trading post DOWNHILL — even across a zero.

concept.body: Quick rewind. Add one spot at a time, ones first. If a spot's sum is **10 or more**, send 10 of it up as 1 (the receipt) and keep the rest. 9 + 4 = 13 → keep 3, send 1 ten up. The receipt ALWAYS gets counted with the next spot.

options.feedback: Ones overflow at 13; the receipt makes the tens 2 + 1 + 1 = 4.
33 lost the receipt — the ten that traded up from 13 ones must be counted: 2 + 1 + 1 tens.
313 wrote all 13 ones into one spot. One digit per spot — ten of the 13 trade up.
